Bayesian false discovery rate selection

Source: R/inference.R
bayes_fdr.Rd

Selects the largest set of hypotheses whose posterior expected false discovery rate is at most alpha, using the direct posterior probability approach (Newton et al. 2004). Hypotheses are ranked by their posterior probability prob; the expected FDR of the top \(k\) is the mean of \(1 - prob\) over them.

Usage

bayes_fdr(prob, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

prob

Numeric vector of posterior probabilities (e.g. posterior inclusion probabilities), or a symmetric matrix of edge probabilities (only the upper triangle is used).

alpha

Target posterior expected FDR. Default 0.05.

Value

A logical vector, or a symmetric logical matrix with FALSE diagonal, marking the selected hypotheses. Attributes: expected_fdr (posterior expected FDR of the selected set, 0 if none), n_selected, cutoff (smallest selected probability, or NA) and alpha.

Details

The guarantee is only as good as the calibration of prob. For differential edges, pass a probability of a real difference such as \(P(|D| > c)\) or \(P(g_k \ne g_m)\), not a sign probability.

Tied probabilities are selected or rejected together: the cutoff is only placed between distinct values of prob, so the selection does not depend on the order of the input. If including a whole block of ties would push the expected FDR above alpha, none of the block is selected.

Missing probabilities are never selected and do not count towards the expected FDR.

References

Newton, M.A., Noueiry, A., Sarkar, D. & Ahlquist, P. (2004). Detecting differential gene expression with a semiparametric hierarchical mixture method. Biostatistics, 5(2), 155-176.

See also

pooled_perm_pvalues() for permutation-based selection.

Examples

bayes_fdr(c(0.99, 0.97, 0.9, 0.6, 0.2), alpha = 0.05)
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE
#> attr(,"expected_fdr")
#> [1] 0.04666667
#> attr(,"n_selected")
#> [1] 3
#> attr(,"cutoff")
#> [1] 0.9
#> attr(,"alpha")
#> [1] 0.05

# Tied probabilities are kept together
bayes_fdr(c(1, 1, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9), alpha = 0.05)
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE
#> attr(,"expected_fdr")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,"n_selected")
#> [1] 2
#> attr(,"cutoff")
#> [1] 1
#> attr(,"alpha")
#> [1] 0.05
